note: Staircase family taxonomy for the Nex 4-layer Q&A architecture (Philip 2026-08-02). Every confirmed image record carries a `families` array listing the families it belongs to. A design can belong to multiple families (e.g. a floating cantilever with a glass balustrade belongs to BOTH `floating-cantilever` AND `glass-balustrade`).

families.label: Spiral staircase (central-column)
families.description: Full-circular spiral around a central steel column. Every tread supported by the column. Traditional 360° rotation.

families.label: Helical staircase (bespoke sculptural)
families.description: Sweeping double-curved sculptural staircase without a central column. Each tread individually engineered. Grand entrance / feature centrepiece.

families.label: Curved mono-stringer staircase
families.description: Single curved fabricated steel stringer carrying the treads. Follows a smooth continuous radius. Contemporary feature.

families.label: Straight mono-stringer staircase
families.description: Single straight steel stringer running down the centre. Modern minimalist. Common in open-plan interiors.

families.label: Floating cantilever staircase
families.description: Treads appear to float · concealed structural steel fixed into wall or hidden frame · open riser · often paired with frameless glass balustrade.

families.label: Straight-flight staircase
families.description: Simple straight run between floors. Cross-cutting geometry family (a straight-flight can also be a mono-stringer or floating cantilever).

families.label: Open-riser staircase
families.description: No solid riser between treads · lets light through · modern appearance · regulatory considerations vary by country.

families.label: Glass balustrade (cross-cutting)
families.description: Any staircase with a structural glass balustrade. Toughened laminated safety glass typical. Cuts across all geometry families.

families.label: Steel balustrade (cross-cutting)
families.description: Any staircase with steel balusters, horizontal rods, or cable systems. Cuts across geometry families.

families.label: Timber balustrade (cross-cutting)
families.description: Any staircase with timber spindles or newels. Cuts across geometry families.

families.label: Integrated feature lighting (cross-cutting)
families.description: Any staircase with integrated LED tread lighting, handrail lighting, or architectural feature lighting. Cuts across geometry and balustrade families.

families.label: Quarter-turn staircase (L-shape)
families.description: Two straight flights with a 90° change of direction, usually joined by an intermediate landing.

families.label: Half-turn staircase (U-shape)
families.description: Two straight flights with a 180° change of direction, joined by a half landing. Also called a switchback.

families.label: Dog-leg staircase
families.description: Two straight parallel flights in opposite directions with a half landing between them. The side profile resembles a dog's rear leg, which is where the name comes from.

families.label: Bifurcated staircase
families.description: A grand staircase where one lower flight divides into two upper flights (or vice versa). From Latin bi + furca = 'two forks'. Common in hotels and grand entrances.

families.label: Winder staircase (tapered-tread turn)
families.description: Direction change achieved with tapered/kite-shaped steps instead of a landing. Saves space and creates a continuous turn.

families.label: Concrete staircase (structural core)
families.description: Staircase whose primary structural support is reinforced concrete — cast in-situ or precast. The concrete forms the structural shell; finishes (timber overlays · stone · tile · glass balustrade) provide the visible architecture. Same universal geometry rules apply as any other staircase — only the structural method changes.

components.label: Tread
components.description: The horizontal step surface. Timber, stone or glass depending on design.

components.label: Riser
components.description: The vertical face between treads. Solid (closed) or absent (open).

components.label: Stringer
components.description: The structural side or centre support carrying the treads. Mono, twin, cut, closed, or box variants.

components.label: Newel post
components.description: The vertical post at the start / end / turn of a staircase. Structural anchor for handrail + balustrade.

components.label: Handrail
components.description: The continuous graspable rail alongside the flight. Timber, steel, brass, bronze, or leather-wrapped.

components.label: Baluster / spindle
components.description: Vertical infill between handrail and tread. Steel, timber, or replaced with glass panels / cable systems.

components.label: Glass balustrade panel
components.description: Toughened laminated glass panel used in place of vertical balusters. Frameless or channel-fixed.

components.label: LED tread / accent lighting
components.description: Integrated LED strip lighting under treads, along stringers, or in handrails.

components.label: Landing
components.description: The horizontal platform at the top / turn of a staircase. Structural connection to upper floor.

components.label: Glass fixings (bolts / standoffs / channels)
components.description: Stainless steel bolts, standoffs, or channel systems that fix structural glass panels to the staircase or floor.
